message.abstract: <jats:p>Accurate offshore wind power forecasting serves as a cornerstone of modern ocean engineering, playing a critical role in ensuring the stability, security, and high-efficiency operation of marine power grids. However, the vast majority of da-ta-driven power forecasting methods rarely account for the constraints of real-world operational scenarios, leading to a lack of physical consistency in offshore wind power mechanisms. Furthermore, compared to time-series foundation mod-els with robust generalization backbones, traditional models exhibit inferior generalization performance across varying time scales. To address these challenges, this study proposes a physics-constrained and generalization-enhanced industri-al large model. First, Chronos-2 is adopted as the backbone with a LoRA strategy to enhance temporal generalization and adaptation under complex maritime conditions. Second, a physics-constrained penalty unit is embedded into a hybrid loss function to ensure outputs follow real-world power boundaries. Experiments on a 350 MW wind farm show that the model maintains an R2 above 0.94 at a 4-hour horizon. An 8-month stress test further demonstrates superior sta-bility and generalization over SVR, LSTM, and SCINet baselines even under seasonal volatility.</jats:p>
title: Physics-Constrained and Generalization-Enhanced Industrial Large Model for Offshore Wind Power Forecasting
